app.name: FirstHour
app.tagline: A calm plan for the first hour after a scam.
disclaimer: FirstHour does not contact your bank, file reports, or promise to recover money.
nothing_saved: Nothing is saved. Print your summary before closing.
start.heading: What happened?
start.evidence: Paste the scam messages, or describe what happened
start.evidence_hint: Optional. You can skip this and still get your plan.
plan.heading: Your plan
plan.out_of_scope: We have full steps only for bank transfers and e-wallets in the last hour. Here are the steps that apply to everyone.
timeline.empty: Nothing yet. Tick a step when you have done it.
banks.label: Your bank
banks.other: Other: use the number on your card or in your bank app
step.call-bank.title: Call your bank's fraud line now
step.call-bank.body: Tell them you were scammed and ask them to stop or recall the transfer. Use the number on the back of your card or in your bank app.
step.report-in-app.title: Report it inside your e-wallet app now
step.report-in-app.body: Open your e-wallet app and use its report or help option to tell the provider you were scammed.
step.call-nsrc.title: Call the National Scam Response Centre: 997
step.call-nsrc.body: The government page lists the line as open daily, 24 hours. Call within 24 hours of finding out so authorities can block accounts and transactions. Older pages said 8 am to 8 pm; if nobody answers, call your bank.
step.police-report.title: Make a police report
step.police-report.body: The official page lists a police report as its own step. Ask the 997 operator whether your call is recorded as a report; if not, go to the nearest police station.
step.semak-mule.title: Check the account number on Semak Mule
step.semak-mule.body: Enter the account number the money went to. A match is a strong warning. No match does not mean the account is safe.
step.no-recovery-fee.title: Never pay anyone to get your money back
step.no-recovery-fee.body: Police say nobody can guarantee recovery for a fee. Offers to recover your money are a second scam. Call 997 or visit a police station instead.
facts.heading: What we found
facts.hint: Each fact shows the line it came from. Fix anything that is wrong; the call script updates.
facts.offline: We could not read your messages. Fill in what you know. Your plan is the same.
script.heading: What to say to your bank
script.english: This script is in English on purpose, so the bank can follow it.
check.heading: Got a message offering to get your money back? Check it.
check.none: No known recovery-scam signs. Never pay to get money back.
check.warning: Warning: this looks like a recovery scam
flag.fee.label: It asks for a fee before returning your money
flag.fee.explain: Police say nobody can guarantee recovery for a fee. Real recovery goes through the police and courts, not an upfront payment.
flag.agent.label: It claims to be an official recovery officer
flag.agent.explain: Police have warned about fake NSRC and police recovery services. Check by calling 997 yourself.
flag.link.label: It sends a link to claim a refund
flag.link.explain: Links to claim a refund are used to steal more money or details. Do not open it.
